tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the RailCore Indian Railways API documentation: guides (authentication, request signing, rate limits, billing in requests), endpoint pages and error codes. Returns the best matching sections with links. Use it for any how-to question about the API.

tools.name: get_endpoint
tools.description: Details of one RailCore API endpoint: method and URL, parameters, what it costs in requests, the key scope it needs, which plans can use it and whether requests must be signed, response fields and the errors it can answer. Accepts an endpoint id (seat-availability), a method and path (GET /trains/{t

tools.name: get_code_sample
tools.description: Working code for a RailCore API endpoint in curl, Node.js, Python, PHP, Go or Java. Set signed to true for Growth, Scale and Enterprise keys, which must sign every request with HMAC-SHA256. Samples read the key from RAILCORE_KEY and the signing secret from RAILCORE_HMAC_SECRET, and work out their da

tools.name: explain_error
tools.description: What a RailCore API error means and how to fix it. Pass the error code (QUOTA_NOT_SUPPORTED), the HTTP status, or the whole error response. Never paste an API key or signing secret; any key-shaped text is removed before it is read.

tools.name: get_plans
tools.description: RailCore API plans: monthly price in INR, requests a month, per minute and per day, which plans must sign requests, IP allowlists, and which include charts and jobs. Pass a plan name to see one plan.

tools.name: get_my_usage
tools.description: Your RailCore API plan and this month's usage: requests used and left, the per-minute and per-day limits, use per API key and in the docs playground, and when the allowance refills. Requires sign-in to your RailCore account.

tools.name: list_my_keys
tools.description: Your active RailCore API keys: label, the first characters of the key, scopes, whether a signing secret is set, how many IP addresses are allowed, and when each was created, last used and expires. Never a full key or secret. Requires sign-in to your RailCore account.

tools.name: try_endpoint
tools.description: Send one real request to a RailCore API read endpoint with your account and return its answer: status, request ID, requests counted and left, and the response body. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_endpoint · Private data: get_code_sample, explain_error, get_my_usage, list_my_keys · Public sink: try_endpoint · Destructive: get_code_sample.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_endpoint · Private data: get_code_sample, explain_error, get_my_usage, list_my_keys · Public sink: try_endpoint · Destructive: get_code_sample

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
